record.paper_title: Open Problems in Efficient Semi-Supervised PAC Learning
record.original_question: Consider the co-training setting in which the hypothesis h is a linear separator and each unlabeled example is a pair (x1, x2). Efficient algorithms are known in the special case where x1 and x2 are drawn independently conditional on their label, but the general consistency problem is NP-hard. The open question is whether one can relax the independence-given-the-label assumption in a nontrivial way and still obtain a computationally efficient algorithm for this class.

evidence.quote: Co-training with linear separators: A generalization of the above problem is the case that h is a linear separator. It is known that the consistency problem is NP-hard [A. Flaxman, personal communication], however efficient algorithms are known for the special case that the elements x1 and x2 of the pair are drawn independently given their label [3, 1]. Even if one cannot solve the problem efficiently in general, a natural question is whether one can at least weaken the independence-given-the-label assumption in a nontrivial way and still get an efficient algorithm for this class.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Co-training setting. Let $X_1, X_2 \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be two "views" of an instance space, and consider a target concept given by a pair of homogeneous linear separators $h_1, h_2$ such that for the relevant distribution $D$ on labeled pairs $((x_1, x_2), y) \in X_1 \times X_2 \times \{-1,+1\}$, with probability 1 the labels agree: $\mathrm{sign}(h_1 \cdot x_1) = \mathrm{sign}(h_2 \cdot x_2) = y$. The learner receives a large sample of unlabeled pairs $(x_1, x_2)$ drawn i.i.d. from the marginal of $D$ on $X_1 \times X_2$ (possibly together with a small amount of labeled data), and must output, in time polynomial in $d, 1/\varepsilon, 1/\delta$, hypotheses whose joint error on $D$ is at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

Known facts: (i) the consistency problem for arbitrary distributions over pairs is NP-hard; (ii) efficient algorithms exist in the special case where $x_1$ and $x_2$ are conditionally independent given the label $y$.

Question. Identify a nontrivial relaxation of the conditional-independence-given-the-label assumption on the joint distribution of $(x_1, x_2)$ under which one can still give a computationally efficient (polynomial-time) PAC-style co-training algorithm that learns a pair of linear separators to arbitrarily small error.
artifact.status_search_result: Blum and Mansour (COLT 2017), "Efficient Co-Training of Linear Separators under Weak Dependence," give a polynomial-time co-training algorithm for homogeneous linear separators under a "weak dependence" condition that strictly relaxes independence-given-the-label, learning from unlabeled data plus one labeled example, for distributions with inverse-polynomial margin and center of mass at the origin. This provides an affirmative answer to the open question.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Co-Training of Linear Separators under Weak Dependence
status_evidence.snippet: first polynomial-time algorithm for co-training of homogeneous linear separators under weak dependence, a relaxation of the condition of independence given the label
status_evidence.claim: A nontrivial relaxation (weak dependence) admits an efficient co-training algorithm for linear separators.
